sources.citation: Pick, Andrew. 2020. A Reconstruction of Proto-Northern Adelbert Phonology and Lexicon. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa.
sources.note: Cited by Glottolog for Sihan subclassification only; the word 'Sihan' does not occur in the text (Northern Adelbert languages only). Irrelevant to Sihan stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Mabuso languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-32. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Sihan is language C5 in ~300-item comparative tables. The transcription note (p. viii, sect. 6) calls the transcription 'semi-phonemic' and lists stop voicing fluctuation, a labio-velar stop, nasalised vowels in Munit, optional initial h; stress is never mentioned and the 140 Sihan rows carry no accent marks.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19.
sources.note: p. 6 (general remark for the whole survey): 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Sihan is NOT among the languages in this study (the Gum family, then called Abaian, comprised Gumalu, Isebe, Amele, Bau; Sihan was surveyed 1971-73).
